sections.h2: Where is Lewiston, Maine, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Lewiston sits in Androscoggin County, roughly halfway between Augusta and Portland, on the east bank of the Androscoggin River. Auburn is directly across the water, and the two cities form one metro area. The city covers about 35.5 square miles, of which roughly 34 are land.

The river drives the layout. The old downtown and the mill district hug the falls, and residential streets climb away from the water. Greene, Sabattus and Lisbon border the city on its other sides, so the edges of Lewiston are more rural than the downtown core.

The 2020 Census counted 37,121 people and 16,579 housing units, with 7.8 percent of those units vacant. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 38,866 residents shows the city growing slowly.

Mill money built most of the older housing. Water power from the Androscoggin led investors to form the Androscoggin Falls Dam, Lock and Canal Company in 1836, and the Bates Mill was finished in 1852. For about three decades it was the largest employer in Maine.

The workers needed somewhere to live. About 400 Irish laborers arrived in 1850 to build the canals, and French Canadian families followed from 1861, settling downtown in the neighborhood known as Little Canada. Lewistown became the city of Lewiston in 1863. Textile mills began closing in the 1950s, and the population fell after 1970.

What that left behind is a lot of multi-family buildings, three-deckers and small wood-frame houses on narrow lots. Many are a century old or more. If you own one, expect a buyer to ask about the roof, knob-and-tube wiring, the heating system and lead paint, and expect repair quotes to affect the price.

  • Older wood-frame houses near downtown often have mixed upgrades from different decades.
  • Three-unit and larger buildings fall under the city's rental registration rules (covered below).
  • Condition varies block by block, so a street-level view matters more than a citywide average.

sections.h2: What does Lewiston's winter mean for a house?
sections.html:
Lewiston has a humid continental climate, so the heating system and the roof take the load. The 1991 to 2020 averages show a January daily high near 28 degrees, a July daily high near 80, and about 45 inches of precipitation a year. The record low is minus 28.

Buyers and inspectors look at the same few things after a Maine winter:

  • Ice dams at roof edges, plus attic insulation and ventilation.
  • Oil tank age and location, and whether the furnace or boiler has been serviced.
  • Frost damage to foundations, porch footings and chimneys.
  • Basement moisture, since the city sits beside a river and spring melt raises the water table.

A house with deferred work in any of these areas is a common reason a conventional sale stalls after inspection. It is also a common reason owners choose a cash sale to a buyer who purchases as-is.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and nearby institutions affect selling in Lewiston?
sections.html:
Lewiston is easy to reach from the Maine Turnpike, which helps buyers who commute. Exit 80 serves the city, Portland is about 40 minutes away, and Boston is about two hours. U.S. Route 202 and state routes 11 and 100 run along Main Street, and the Citylink bus system serves Lewiston and Auburn.

Public schools are run by Lewiston Public Schools, which includes Lewiston High School, Lewiston Middle School, five elementary schools and a regional technical center. Higher education adds steady rental and buyer demand. Bates College is in the city, the University of Southern Maine has a Lewiston-Auburn campus, and Central Maine Community College is across the river in Auburn.

Auburn/Lewiston Municipal Airport handles general aviation. Most commercial travelers use the Portland Jetport.

sections.h2: How does Lewiston property tax affect a sale?
sections.html:
Lewiston's mil rate is above $30 and the city is in the middle of a revaluation, so tax is a real part of the selling conversation. The city's Assessor's page lists mil rates of $31.77 for fiscal 2025, $32.78 for fiscal 2026 and $34.15 for fiscal 2027, per $1,000 of assessed value.

The last citywide revaluation took effect in 1988. The state found Lewiston's assessments too low compared with sales, so the city hired Tyler Technologies of Yarmouth. Notices of proposed value, based on fair market value as of April 1, 2026 and 28 months of sales data, were mailed April 24, 2026. The council asked for a one-year delay, and the Assessor's page says the new values will be implemented for the 2027 tax year, which is the 2028 fiscal year.

For a seller, the practical point is that your current bill is based on old values. A buyer will look at the new value, not only the bill you hand them.

sections.h2: What happens if property tax goes unpaid on a Lewiston house?
sections.html:
Maine uses a lien process that can end in automatic foreclosure, and the clock is long enough that a sale can usually still fix it. Under 36 M.R.S. section 942, the tax collector may send a demand notice between 8 months and one year after commitment, giving 30 days to pay. If the tax stays unpaid, a tax lien certificate is recorded at the registry of deeds.

Recording creates a tax lien mortgage with priority over other mortgages and liens. Under section 943, if the tax, interest and costs are not paid within 18 months of the filing, the lien is deemed foreclosed and the right of redemption ends. The treasurer must send notice 30 to 45 days before that date.

  • Selling during the redemption period pays the lien off from proceeds at closing.
  • If a seller has paid a pro rata share of the tax under a written proration agreement, the treasurer can record a certificate saying so.
  • Hardship abatement is available for a primary residence under 36 M.R.S. section 841(2), with a written decision due within 30 days.

An error or illegality abatement application must be filed within 185 days of commitment, so owners who think a value is wrong should not wait.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and recording fees apply when selling in Lewiston?
sections.html:
Maine charges a real estate transfer tax of $2.20 for each $500 of value, and the buyer and seller each pay half. For a sale up to $1 million, that works out to $1.10 per $500 from each side. For transfers on or after November 1, 2025, an extra $3.80 per $500 applies to value above $1 million, which rarely affects Lewiston homes.

Recording a deed costs $40 for most submitters, according to the Maine Registries of Deeds fee page. The deed and a transfer tax form go to the county registry, and the form must state any exemption. Maine Revenue Services publishes the rules.

sections.h2: Do Lewiston landlords and sellers of rentals need to register?
sections.html:
Yes, buildings with three or more units must be registered with the city. The requirement applies even if the owner lives in one of the units, and it does not cover two-unit buildings. There is no registration fee, but unregistered buildings can face civil penalties and are not eligible for city-administered loans or grants.

Newly built multi-family buildings must register within 30 days of the certificate of occupancy. Council agendas in 2026 listed amendments to the article, so confirm the current wording with the City Clerk at 207-513-3124.

The Planning and Code Enforcement Department, at 207-513-3125, enforces the Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code, which the city has applied since September 28, 2011. Open permits and unfinished work are worth clearing up before you list.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house fast in Lewiston?
sections.html:
The three realistic routes are a listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a cash offer, and they trade time against price. A listing usually brings the highest price for a house in good shape, but it adds showings, inspection negotiations and a buyer's financing timeline. A for-sale-by-owner sale saves commission but moves the marketing and contract work onto you.

A cash sale to a company like ours removes the repair and financing steps. We buy as-is, so a Lewiston house with an old roof, a tenant or an unpaid tax lien can still sell. The offer is usually lower than a perfectly prepared retail sale, and you should compare it against your net after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

  • Check your tax balance with the Treasury office first.
  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff and a list of tenants if there are any.
  • Ask for the offer in writing and read who pays each closing cost.

faqs.q: How much is the Lewiston tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's Assessor's page lists $34.15 per $1,000 of assessed value for fiscal 2027, up from $32.78 in fiscal 2026 and $31.77 in fiscal 2025.

faqs.q: When do new Lewiston property values take effect?
faqs.a: The Assessor's page says the citywide revaluation will be implemented for the 2027 tax year, which is fiscal 2028. The new proposed values reflect fair market value as of April 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lewiston house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and lien costs are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Under Maine law a recorded tax lien mortgage is deemed foreclosed 18 months after filing if unpaid, so earlier action gives you more options.

faqs.q: Who pays the Maine transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer and seller split it equally. The rate is $2.20 per $500 of value, with an extra $3.80 per $500 on the portion above $1 million for transfers on or after November 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a Lewiston duplex as a rental?
faqs.a: No. The city's rental registration applies to buildings with three or more units. A two-unit building is outside it, though you should confirm with the City Clerk because the ordinance was under amendment in 2026.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about my Lewiston assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Department at 207-513-3122 or visit 27 Pine Street. The office is open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 7:45 AM to 4 PM and Tuesday 7:45 AM to 5:30 PM, and closed Friday.
